reason: The donut, large clearly labeled bars and polished phone layout feel more finished than the plainer, more generic right page.
Per-day bars colored by weekday versus weekend with inline annotations show the pattern more clearly than the left's single-color charts, and it holds up well on phone.
Best/worst highlighting in the table and four small-multiple scatter plots tell the rainfall-yield story better, despite the intentionally scrollable table on phone.
Stacked bars with in-bar values and last-year markers plus a diverging change chart are clearer than the left's truncated labels and meaningless 100% column.
The hero margin card, revenue-share stacked bars and large annotated margin line chart are more polished and legible than the left's tables and small charts.
The navy masthead, serif body, pull-quote and contact card give a properly designed press-release look that the left's generic card layout lacks.
Icon tiles, numbered claim steps, jump chips and a closing contact callout make it far more finished than the plain bulleted left page.
The drop cap, pull-quote and numbered advice cards give the essay a more crafted editorial hierarchy than the right's undifferentiated text.
Stacked bills breakdown bars and tier bar make the bill easier to grasp, though a clipped label on phone is a minor flaw against the right's plain tables.
The left's timeline dots overlap the first letters of each schedule item, a visible defect, while the right is clean and readable on both widths.
